Application Materials.content:
When you have completed and submitted the application form, Lancaster will determine the documents needed to assess your application based on the information provided. These will appear in the supporting document section of your application; required documents are marked with a **\*** and must be uploaded for the application to be considered. If documents are not in English, you must provide an official English translation and the untranslated copy.
Information usually required:
- **Academic transcript and degree certificate:** upload an official copy of your degree transcript showing the subjects studied, marks, and confirmation of degree award. If studies are not complete, provide an interim transcript. If studying outside the UK and the university grading scale is not detailed on the transcript, provide the grading scale.
- **Personal statement:** explain why you are applying for the course, what you hope to gain from your studies, and how it fits with your plans. Lancaster recommends a maximum of **500 words**.
- **References:** for Postgraduate Taught applications, provide **one reference**, ideally from someone who can comment on suitability for academic study, such as a tutor from previous studies. A professional reference may be accepted if an academic reference cannot be provided.
- **Proof of English language ability:** depending on where you have studied and your nationality, you may need to provide a recognised English language qualification and upload a copy of your English language certificate.
- **Passport (international applicants only):** submit a copy of your passport if you are an international student and need a student visa to study in the UK.
For most postgraduate programmes, current Lancaster students or alumni will not need to provide a reference, a copy of their transcript, or a personal statement; Lancaster will say if additional documents are needed.

Application Deadlines.content: **Applications for entry in 2027 will open in September 2026.**

Academic Requirements.content:
**2:2 Hons degree** (UK or equivalent) in Psychology, Data Science, Computer Science, Sociology, Criminology, Human Geography, Politics, Law, Management and Marketing, Linguistics. Your degree needs to have covered some Research Methods and Data Analysis modules.
Applicants from diverse backgrounds are welcomed, including computer science, business, sociology, criminology and many more; you don’t need a psychology degree to apply.
For China applicants:
| | 1st | 2:1 | 2:2 |
|------------------|------------|------------|------------|
| Bachelor's degree | 75% to 80% | 70% to 75% | 65% to 70% |
The grade required will vary depending on the University awarding the degree.

English Proficiency Requirements.content: We require an **IELTS (Academic) Test** with an overall score of at least **6.5**, and a minimum of **6.0 in each element** of the test. We also consider [other English language qualifications](https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/study/international-students/english-requirements/requirements-p2/) and if your score is below our requirements, you may be eligible for one of our [pre-sessional English language programmes](https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/study/international-students/pre-sessional-english-language/postgraduate-students/).

Program Overview.content:
Psychology and Behavioural Analytics MSc, entry year 2026, is delivered full time over 1 year.
Top reasons to study include:
- A powerful combination of psychological tools applied to data analysis
- Placement-based dissertation, graduating with demonstrable experience on your CV
- Approved as postgraduate research training by the Economic and Social Research Council
Digital data now dominates all aspects of our lives. Every action we take – from smartphone use to social media activity, public surveillance and even our online purchases – leaves a digital trace. Analysing digital data tells one story, but it isn’t enough to fully understand human behaviour. To do that, you need the insights that psychology provides. The MSc Psychology and Behavioural Analytics integrates psychological insights with an understanding of digital data. You will develop a specialised skill set highly sought after in today’s data-driven world, which will set you apart in the job market, opening new career opportunities.
**Who is this programme for?** Anyone who wants to understand digital data through human psychology. We welcome individuals from diverse backgrounds, including computer science, business, sociology, criminology and many more. You don’t need a psychology degree to apply.
Taught by world-leading academics, you will develop a rare combination of technical data analysis and psychological expertise, providing a broader perspective to tackle a wide range of professional challenges. You will also:
- Develop key critical thinking and communication skills, allowing you to evaluate data and convey your findings to a range of audiences
- Develop your skills with data analysis software such as R, Python, Nvivo and BORIS
- Enhance your skills in qualitative and quantitative research methods to analyse both individual experiences and large-scale trends
- Undertake a placement-based dissertation, allowing you to apply and develop your skills towards impactful, real-world projects
- Learn how to ethically and responsibly handle digital data
Through a dynamic mix of data science and psychology-focused modules, you will gain hands-on experience with various types of digital data, including visual data such as CCTV footage, body-cam videos and social media; natural language such as social media posts, blogs and online forums; and mobile sensor data such as movement tracking, sound and usage logs. You will build a strong foundation in key psychological concepts related to behaviour, including identity, personality and cognitive decision-making. Important topics are covered, such as data limitations, bias and the principles of responsible research.
The final term is where everything comes together with your dissertation. Gain valuable, practical experience working on a project with either a partner organisation or within the Department of Psychology. The programme provides dedicated support to guide you through the process, ensuring you gain relevant experience that will make you stand out to employers.
Students have investigated how CCTV recordings can provide insight into bystander behaviour and behavioural biometrics from digital footprint data, such as mobile phone usage. Staff are involved in the Policing Academic Centre of Excellence, providing links to digital data in policing practices.
The programme is in the Department of Psychology, Faculty of Science and Technology.
Careers: The master’s in Psychology and Behavioural Analytics opens the door to a wide range of career paths. The qualitative and quantitative insights you will be able to provide make you a valuable asset to any employer. Roles of interest may include social researcher, data analyst, behavioural analyst, data scientist, AI trainer, market research analyst, human resources specialist and customer experience analyst. You may also use this master’s as a stepping stone for further study, including a career in academia as either a lecturer or researcher.

Curriculum.content:
Duration: **Full time 1 year**.
Course structure: Core modules include:
- **Advanced Modelling with Psychological Data**: Apply advanced analysis methods to psychological data, including handling large-scale, rich and sometimes messy real-life datasets, constructing models, presenting evidence-based visualisations, coding in R, and working in a team.
- **Analysing Talk and Text**: Introduction to qualitative and quantitative approaches to analysing talk and text, structured around conducting a research project. Topics include Natural language processing; Thematic Analysis and Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA); Conversation analysis and discursive approaches; Quantitative analysis through Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC); Sentiment analysis and its applications.
- **Digital Data Applications**: Interdisciplinary psychology and computer science module in a laboratory environment, using tools such as R, Python, Java MakeCode, BORIS and Netlogo. Covers digital data types such as video, sensor data and digital trace data, with methods including data cleaning, predictive modelling, behavioural coding and data visualisation.
- **Programming for Health Data Science**: Teaches fundamentals of computing and programming in R and Python, including structured programming, data structures, functions, data file input/output, selection and filtering, exploratory graphics, project management for data and code, reproducible research, source code management, NumPy and Pandas, and plotting basic graphics.
- **Psychological Perspectives and Digital Behavioural Data**: Explores meta-level issues in psychology and behavioural analytics, including psychological theories, digital data, research ethics, morality and scientific practice.
- **Psychology and Behavioural Analytics Dissertation**: A **three-month dissertation project** involving a substantial research project intended to tackle a real-world challenge. Students may undertake a project through an external placement with an industrial or research organisation working in partnership with the University, or carry out an academic project. The project includes completing a comprehensive literature review, formulating testable research hypotheses or defining parameters of an explorative analysis, conducting empirical work, and analysing and interpreting data.
- **Understanding Humans Through Data**: Applies core analytic methods across psychological research and practice settings through lectures and practical workshops, building coding capacity in R. Covers statistical tests, data analysis and processing tools, analysis approaches for testing predictions, describing findings through text and visualisations, and translating data analysis findings into psychological insights.

Cost of Attendance.content:
Below is a rough guide to some average monthly living costs (excluding tuition fees) for a single student in pounds sterling. The exact amount you need to live on will depend on your individual needs and prices at the time. The 2025 [SavetheStudent survey](https://www.savethestudent.org/money/surveys/student-money-survey-2025-results.html) showed an average monthly spend by the survey participants as £1142 per month (including accommodation). In addition to the costs below, there may be initial "start-up" costs which might vary according to what you are able to bring with you, or there may be unforeseen costs. If you are an international student and require a [student visa](https://www.gov.uk/search?q=student+visa) to study in the UK, you will also have to comply with the minimum funding required for this.
- **Groceries:** £146 per month*
- **Bills:** £69 per month*
- **Going out:** £61 per month*
- **Transport:** £67 per month*
- **Takeaways and eating out:** £49 per month*
- **Clothes and shopping:** £40 per month*
- **Holidays and events:** £32 per month*
- **Health and Wellbeing:** £24 per month*
- **Other:** £26 per month*
- **Mobile Phone:** £15 per month*
- **Course Materials:** £20 per month*
- **Gifts and Charity:** £17 per month*
- **Friends and family:** £17 per month*
- **Rent:** £529 per month*
*please note these figures represent single students, rather than students with families.
**Insurance**: Insurance costs vary depending on the cover required, there are several online comparison websites online. Rent on campus [includes limited cover](http://www.cover4insurance.com/lancaster-university).
**Laundry**: the campus laundrette each standard wash is £3.00* (+50p for super wash, +£1 for super plus cycle) and each tumble dry is £1.70*. You will need to buy your own laundry washing products. (*prices subject to change in new academic year.)
**Campus Accommodation:** If you will be [living on campus](https://portal.lancaster.ac.uk/ask/campus/living-in-university-accommodation/) check out the [accommodation pages](https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/accommodation/) to see cost and what is included.

Financial Aid.content:
- Lancaster Master's Excellence Scholarship: available for eligible applicants to all full-time Postgraduate Taught degree programmes, offered fully on campus by Lancaster University, for 2026 entry. The scholarship amount awarded varies by the programme fee level and the grade of your undergraduate degree at the point of entry. You will be automatically considered for this funding when you apply. The value of the award will be confirmed when your offer is made unconditional and will be awarded as a tuition fee reduction.
- Science and Technology Master’s Excellence Scholarship: up to 30% of your programme fee. The Science and Technology Master’s Excellence Scholarship offers a range of awards of up to £9,000 to both home and international fee-paying students who are applying to study a taught postgraduate master’s programme offered full time, on campus, starting in 2026. You will automatically be considered if you have an average grade to date at a 1st (home and international), or 2:1 level (international) in your undergraduate studies, or have already achieved a 1st (home and international), or 2:1 (international) degree, and accept a conditional or unconditional offer from Lancaster University for 2026 entry.
- If an applicant is eligible for both awards, this scholarship can be combined with the Alumni Loyalty Scholarship. If successfully awarded a named departmental scholarship, it can be combined with this scholarship. This scholarship cannot be combined with the International Regional Scholarship – Postgraduate.
- Other scholarships and bursaries include: [Postgraduate International Regional Scholarship](https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/scholarships-and-bursaries/pg-international-regional-scholarship/), [India Scholarship- Postgraduate](https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/scholarships-and-bursaries/india-scholarship-postgraduate/), [Postgraduate International Study Centre Progress](https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/scholarships-and-bursaries/postgraduate-international-study-centre-progression-scholarship/), [Alumni Loyalty Scholarship](https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/scholarships-and-bursaries/alumni-loyalty-scholarship/) (10% off fees for all Taught Master's degrees if you are a Lancaster graduate), [Lancaster Sanctuary Scholarship](https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/scholarships-and-bursaries/lancaster-sanctuary-scholarship/), and [Master’s Scholarship for Black British Students](https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/scholarships-and-bursaries/masters-scholarship-for-black-british-students/) (full fee waiver and stipend of £9,000 for living costs).

Multiple Applications.content: Our online application system allows you to apply for more than one course.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: Requests for a deferral will be considered on a case-by-case basis. If you would like to defer your offer you will need to request this by using our [postgraduate application portal](https://www.e-res.lancaster.ac.uk/postgraduate-applications/Account/Login) or you can [contact us](mailto:pgadmissions@lancaster.ac.uk) by email. If you are requesting a deferral to the following academic year we will not consider your application until we start to make decisions on applications for that year of entry, so it may take a while for a decision to be made on your application.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
Your offer will be either **Conditional** or **Unconditional**:
- **Conditional** means that you have not yet met Lancaster University's academic, English language or any other entry requirements. Details of the offer conditions and how you can meet these requirements will be in the offer letter.
- You can accept your offer before you have met the conditions; you do not need to wait until your offer is unconditional.
- The deadline for meeting the conditions is in the offer letter. If you need longer, you should [let Lancaster know](mailto:pgadmissions@lancaster.ac.uk).
- You may have an offer conditional on more than one qualification, for example, you may need to complete your university studies and take an English language test. You do not have to meet all the conditions at the same time.
- Academic conditions: your transcript and certificate need to be official copies, and if not in English you will also need to provide an official translation. Your transcript needs to state your name, course studied, marks for each subject, dates studied and confirmation that you have completed your studies.
- English language conditions: if you need to sit an English Language test to meet the conditions of your offer, you should do this as soon as possible and upload your score to the [postgraduate application portal](https://www.e-res.lancaster.ac.uk/postgraduate-applications/Account/Login).
- If your English score does not meet the conditions of the offer, Lancaster will automatically consider your eligibility for one of its [pre-sessional English language courses](https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/study/entry-requirements/pre-sessional-english/) and contact you by email if this is an option. Lancaster cannot consider you for a pre-sessional course without seeing a valid English language score, and does not accept pre-sessional courses delivered by other organisations or institutions.
- For applicants who need a student visa, the CAS process cannot start until the offer is unconditional and Lancaster has received passport details.
